title.en: Australia news live: petrol back above $2 a litre in some areas; warning of more bird flu spread as local transmission confirmed
title.zh: 澳大利亚新闻直播：部分地区汽油价格回升至每升2澳元以上；禽流感传播警告，当地已确认传播

summary.en: Reports indicate that petrol prices have risen above $2 a litre in some Australian regions, while authorities have confirmed local transmission of bird flu, warning of further spread. Separately, a specially modified Airbus A350 completed a 24-hour test flight before joining the Qantas fleet.
summary.zh: 报道称，澳大利亚部分地区的汽油价格已回升至每升2澳元以上，同时当局已确认禽流感在当地传播，并警告可能进一步扩散。此外，一架经过特殊改装的空客A350飞机在完成24小时的创纪录试飞后，将加入澳洲航空机队。

body.en:
Petrol is back above $2 a litre and diesel prices have hit $2.40 in some cities as fuel costs race upwards.

Oil prices have steadily risen since the US resumed strikes on Iran, with Brent crude up from about US$70 on 2 July to US$87 today, while the Australian government reduced its fuel excise discount by 16 cents a litre.

Melbourne is facing diesel prices of $2.40 a litre today, up 66 cents from their June low of 173.9c/L, according to Motormouth. Canberra is at 238c/L, Brisbane is at 234.4, Adelaide at 233.7, Sydney 232.8, and 226.4 in Perth.

Unleaded petrol prices have risen to 204.1 cents a litre in Canberra. They’re at 195.6c/L in Melbourne, 195.2 in Brisbane, 192.6 in Adelaide and 191.1, in Sydney – the latter up from its June low of 152.2. Perth has seen the biggest jump, with unleaded at 196.6c/L today, up nearly 50 cents from the June low of 148.3.
body.zh: 随着燃料成本的上涨，一些城市的汽油价格重新回到每升 2 美元以上，柴油价格已达到 2.40 美元。 自美国恢复对伊朗打击以来，油价稳步上涨，布伦特原油从7月2日的约70美元上涨至今天的87美元，而澳大利亚政府将燃油消费税折扣降低了16美分/升。 据 Motormouth 称，墨尔本今天的柴油价格为每升 2.40 澳元，比 6 月份的低点 173.9c/L 上涨了 66 美分。堪培拉为 238c/L，布里斯班为 234.4，阿德莱德为 233.7，悉尼为 232.8，珀斯为 226.4。 堪培拉无铅汽油价格已上涨至每升 204.1 美分。墨尔本的气温为 195.6c/L，布里斯班为 195.2c/L，阿德莱德为 192.6c/L，悉尼为 191.1c/L，后者高于 6 月份的低点 152.2。珀斯的涨幅最大，今天无铅汽油价格为 196.6 美分/升，较 6 月低点 148.3 美分上涨近 50 美分。

reflection.en: In a world filled with news of rising costs and health concerns, it's easy for anxiety to take root. This verse reminds us to bring all our worries to Yahweh in prayer, finding peace beyond understanding. Even amidst daily uncertainties, we can choose to trust in His care.
reflection.zh: 在一个充满物价上涨和健康担忧新闻的世界里，焦虑很容易滋生。这节经文提醒我们，要将所有的忧虑藉着祷告带到雅伟面前，寻得超乎理解的平安。即使在日常的不确定性中，我们也能选择信靠祂的看顾。

verse.textEn: Do not be anxious about anything, but in every situation, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, present your requests to God.
verse.textZh: 应当一无挂虑，只要凡事藉着祷告、祈求和感谢，将你们所要的告诉神。

title.en: Rescue teams face ‘race against time’ in search for trapped survivors as death toll in Japan rises to at least 13 – live updates
title.zh: 日本地震死亡人数上升，救援队争分夺秒搜寻幸存者

summary.en: Emergency workers are continuing their search for survivors in southern Japan after yesterday’s powerful earthquake, as the death toll rises and teams face a 'race against time' to find those trapped.
summary.zh: 在日本南部发生强烈地震后，紧急救援人员正继续搜寻幸存者，死亡人数不断上升，救援队正争分夺秒地寻找被困人员。

At least 13 people have been killed and many reported missing after the earthquake struck the Kumamoto area on the southern main island of Kyushu with a magnitude of 7.1, according to the Japan meteorological agency. Psalm 46:1 reminds us that Yahweh is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in times of trouble. This truth offers a steady anchor for those trapped, for the tireless rescue teams, and for all who grieve and hope.

title.en: Saudi Arabia joins US in strikes on Iran-backed militia
title.zh: 伊朗和美国互发袭击，打破短暂平静

summary.en: US Central Command reported intercepting multiple ballistic missiles launched by Iran, marking a renewed exchange of hostilities after a brief period of calm.
summary.zh: 美国中央司令部报告称，拦截了伊朗发射的多枚弹道导弹，这标志着在短暂的平静之后，敌对行动再次升级。

body.en:
Saudi Arabia has joined the US in carrying out strikes against an Iran-backed militia in Iraq, in a potential escalation of the Middle East conflict.

US Central Command (Centcom) said the strikes were against "Iran-aligned terrorists that the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) directed to attack US forces and Saudi energy infrastructure".

The statement did not name the militia. However, the Popular Mobilisation Forces (PMF) said at least 10 of its members had been killed.

It comes after Iran launched "multiple" ballistic missiles in an "attempted surprise attack" on American forces in the Middle East, according to Centcom. The exchange ends a brief break in US-Iran hostilities.

The US said the attack occurred at 17:45 EDT (21:45 GMT) on Tuesday, with all missiles "successfully intercepted". Iran said it had targeted a US base in Jordan.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) also said it had hit three oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, according to the Tasnim News Agency.

Centcom said US and Saudi fighter jets had struck "multiple terrorist logistics and weapons sites across eastern Iraq in a strong response to over 30 IRGC-directed aerial drone attacks in the last 72 hours".

"The IRGC and its terrorist proxies must cease these attacks to avoid further U.S. military response," the Centcom statement said.

The PMF said the US-Saudi attacks were "a dangerous escalation" as well as a violation of Iraq's sovereignty.

The PMF is an umbrella organisation that contains several pro-Iranian militias that are part of the network of proxies Tehran has used to advance its interests across the Middle East for years.

Those militias have attacked US personnel and interests in Iraq on a number of occasions, aiming to force the remaining US troops to leave the country. The US has regularly struck back at the militias.

On Tuesday, Saudi Arabia said its military had intercepted and destroyed drones targeting petroleum facilities in the country's eastern region.

Defence ministry spokesman Maj Gen Turki al-Maliki alleged the drones were launched by Iran-affiliated militia groups in Iraqi territory.

The reignited hostilities come two days after US President Donald Trump spoke of "very friendly negotiations" with Iran. At that point, the two sides had not exchanged strikes for a third consecutive day.

The pause in fighting had followed 13 straight nights of bombing by the US, which said it had destroyed tunnels and bridges in southern Iran. Scores of people were reported to have died in the strikes.

Access and control of the Strait of Hormuz remains a key sticking point in talks, which Tehran has denied are even happening.

title.en: The 'final frontier' of travelling is here. But one ritual is far from over
title.zh: 旅行的“最终前沿”已至，但一项仪式远未结束

summary.en: A test flight successfully completed a 24-hour non-stop journey, marking a significant advancement in long-haul air travel and raising questions about the future of traditional stopovers.
summary.zh: 一架测试航班成功完成了24小时不间断飞行，标志着长途航空旅行的重大进步，并引发了关于传统中途停留未来走向的讨论。

body.en:
A record-breaking test flight lasting more than 24 hours has touched down in France from Melbourne — and experts say Australia could be leading the world on the new technology use.

Qantas' specially adapted Airbus A350-1000ULR landed in France on Tuesday after a marathon 24 hours and 24 minutes in the air, covering 23,057km without stopping — the longest direct flight ever attempted by a commercial aircraft.

The flight is part of a two-month test campaign as part of Qantas' Project Sunrise, which aims to launch the world's longest commercial passenger flight and reshape long-haul travel by offering direct flights from Australia's east coast to London and New York.

The previous record belonged to a Boeing 777-200LR, which flew 21,601.7km from Hong Kong to London in 22 hours and 42 minutes back in 2005.

Qantas has ordered 12 of the modified A350 aircraft, each fitted with an extra 20,000-litre fuel tank and configured to seat 238 passengers.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The first is due for delivery in April 2027, with daily non-stop flights between Sydney and London planned from October that year — turning what was once a five-day journey in 1947 on the old 'Kangaroo Route' into a single hop of 19 to 21 hours, depending on winds and routing.

The airline has said a Sydney-New York route will follow shortly after the launch of the London route.

The test flight's success has cast eyes towards the future of air travel, with some wondering whether stopovers in Singapore, Dubai or Los Angeles may be a thing of the past.

Justin Brownjohn from RMIT University's Aviation Academy says non-stop routes will keep becoming more viable as aircraft range improves and fuel use falls — but that doesn't make them a replacement for one-stop flying.

"Airlines have historically competed on network and frequency, but Project Sunrise competes on time," he said.

"Cutting up to four hours off the journey from Sydney to London and removing the connection entirely is a different product, not an improved version of the existing one.

Brownjohn expects the strongest demand for the ultra-long-haul services to come from business and premium leisure travellers willing to pay more for the time saved — and says the wider effect may be felt most by the Middle Eastern and Asian hub airports that have built their business models around the layover.

Spending over 20 hours in the air also raises real questions about passenger wellbeing.

"Twenty hours is not a longer flight, it is a different physiological event," Brownjohn said. "On this flight comfort has stopped being a luxury feature and become the thing being sold."

title.en: Zack Polanski will not say sorry to Farage for sharing ‘dangerous’ image
title.zh: 扎克·波兰斯基拒绝就分享“危险”图片向法拉奇道歉

summary.en: Green party leader Zack Polanski stated he made an “inadvertent mistake” by sharing a social media image but refused to apologize to Nigel Farage. Polanski indicated he would apologize if Farage first apologized for past actions that allegedly endangered people.
summary.zh: 绿党领袖扎克·波兰斯基表示，他因分享一张社交媒体图片犯了“无心之失”，但拒绝向奈杰尔·法拉奇道歉。波兰斯基表示，如果法拉奇首先为过去据称危及他人的行为道歉，他会很乐意道歉。

body.en: Green party leader says it was ‘a mistake’ and if Farage wants to apologise for times he’s put people in danger, he’ll be happy to say sorry The Green party leader, Zack Polanski, has said he made an “inadvertent mistake” over a social media image but will not apologise to Nigel Farage. The image, which Polanski said he “shared inadvertently” on Instagram and then removed, featured a man wearing a black T-shirt with the message “We’re only making plans for Nigel” and an image of a guillotine. Continue reading...
body.zh: 绿党领导人表示这是“一个错误”，如果法拉奇想为他多次将人们置于危险之中而道歉，他会很乐意道歉。绿党领导人扎克·波兰斯基表示，他在社交媒体图片上犯了“无意的错误”，但不会向奈杰尔·法拉奇道歉。波兰斯基称这张照片是他“不经意间”在 Instagram 上分享的，随后被删除，照片中一名男子穿着一件黑色 T 恤，上面写着“我们只是为奈杰尔制定计划”，还有一张断头台的图片。继续阅读...

reflection.en: In public life, words carry immense weight, and a simple apology can often de-escalate tension. This exchange highlights the challenge of humility and the tendency to meet accusation with counter-accusation, which only prolongs conflict. Yahweh's wisdom reminds us that a gentle response has the power to calm anger, while harsh words only fuel the fire.
reflection.zh: 在公共生活中，言语举足轻重，一句简单的道歉常能化解紧张。这起事件凸显了谦卑的挑战，以及人们倾向于以指责回应指责，这只会延长冲突。雅伟的智慧提醒我们，温柔的回答能平息怒气，而严厉的言语只会火上浇油。

verse.textEn: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.
verse.textZh: 回答柔和，使怒消退；言语暴戾，触动怒气。

title.en: Young Liberal power brokers created ‘shit sheet’ on NSW minister accusing him of extramarital affair

summary.zh: 一份据称由年轻的自由党权力掮客制作的、指控新南威尔士州部长婚外情的文档，在一次反腐听证会上被披露。该部长大卫·埃利奥特否认了这些指控。

reflection.en: This incident highlights the profound impact words can have, especially when used to attack someone's character or reputation in the public sphere. Yahweh's wisdom reminds us that our words carry the power of life and death, shaping outcomes and relationships. It calls us to consider the ethical weight of our speech and its potential consequences.
reflection.zh: 这起事件凸显了言语可能造成的深远影响，尤其是在公共领域中用于攻击他人品格或名誉之时。雅伟的智慧提醒我们，我们的言语承载着生死的力量，塑造着结果和人际关系。这呼吁我们深思言语的伦理分量及其潜在后果。

verse.textEn: The tongue has the power of life and death, and those who love it will eat its fruit.
verse.textZh: 生死在舌头的权下；喜爱它的，必吃它所结的果子。

title.en: Japan in a ‘race against time’ to rescue people trapped beneath rubble after quake
title.zh: 日本与时间赛跑，营救地震废墟下的被困者

summary.en: At least 13 people have been killed after the earthquake struck the island of Kyushu on Tuesday.
summary.zh: 周二九州岛发生地震，造成至少13人死亡。

body.en:
At least 13 people have been killed after a 6.8 earthquake struck the island of Kyushu on Tuesday, with some people still missing and thousands displaced from their homes.

BBC’s Jake Kwon explains what has happened in the 24 hours following the initial quake - and why the death toll is expected to rise.
body.zh: 九州岛周二发生 6.8 级地震，已造成至少 13 人死亡，部分人失踪，数千人流离失所。 BBC 的杰克·权 (Jake Kwon) 解释了最初地震后 24 小时内发生的情况，以及预计死亡人数为何会上升。

reflection.en: In the wake of such a devastating earthquake, the thought of people trapped beneath rubble evokes deep concern and fear. Psalm 23:4 reminds us that even in the darkest valleys of life, Yahweh's presence offers comfort and courage. For those grieving loss and those working tirelessly in rescue efforts, may this truth bring a measure of peace amidst the...
reflection.zh: 在如此毁灭性的地震之后，人们被困在瓦砾下的情景令人深感担忧和恐惧。诗篇23:4提醒我们，即使在生命最黑暗的幽谷中，雅伟的同在也能带来安慰和勇气。愿这真理为那些悲伤的人和那些在救援工作中不懈努力的人，在紧迫和悲痛中带来一丝平安。

verse.textEn: Even though I walk through the darkest valley, I will fear no evil, for you are with me.
verse.textZh: 我虽然行过死荫的幽谷，也不怕遭害，因为你与我同在。

title.en: 'I thought I would die': Survivors describe the shock and horror of powerful Japan earthquake
title.zh: “我以为我会死”：幸存者描述日本强震的震惊与恐惧

summary.en: Rescue operations are ongoing in Japan following a 6.8-magnitude earthquake, as survivors recount their experiences of shock and horror.
summary.zh: 日本发生6.8级地震后，救援行动正在进行中，幸存者们讲述了他们所经历的震惊和恐惧。

body.en:
Business was winding down for the day at Sendan Shokudo, a diner in Japan's southwestern city of Yatsushiro, when the whole building suddenly lurched.

Everything on the kitchen shelves cascaded to the floor; bowls and glasses shattered.

"I was surprised, and scared," she told BBC News. "I went under one of the tables right away, but the table moved sharply towards the right, left, right, left, with me."

The area is located on an active tectonic fault system and is no stranger to tremors. In 2016, a pair of earthquakes killed 277 people and injured 2,800 others.

"The last quake 10 years ago was nothing like this one," she said. "I thought I would die."

At least 13 people have been killed in the wake of the 6.8-magnitude earthquake that hit Kumamoto late on Tuesday.

Three of them are from the Aeon shopping mall in Kumamoto city, where dozens are still believed to be trapped.

Rescue efforts are underway, but Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has warned that emergency services are in a "race against time".

Just a few hundred metres away from the Aeon mall, Yui* was sitting in the back office of her cake shop when the quake hit.

"I couldn't tell which was the sound of the earthquake and which was the sound of the explosion," she told the BBC.

"All I could do was hold the chair I was sitting in as big jolts came one after another," she added, appearing to still be in shock.

"I didn't know what to feel; I couldn't even feel scared in such a situation. Even now I don't know what to feel, and I don't know how to explain."

Authorities and emergency responders mobilised quickly. Shortly after the tremor struck, Takaichi put 4,600 personnel on the ground to assist with recovery, and said that teams would work "tirelessly through the night" to assess and monitor the damage in affected areas.

Despite this, tens of thousands of people have experienced power and water outages across Kumamoto City and at least 45 medical facilities have been damaged.

The exterior walls of the 17th century Kumamoto Castle, in the city's centre, came toppling down in a plume of dust. The worship hall of the 19th Century Yatshushiro Shrine completely collapsed.

One local resident Michal Posan said there is "no water or food left in the stores".

Posan, 25, has been living in Kumamoto for two years, and was at home at the time of the quake.

"My TV fell on me, my mirror smashed and the roads around me were damaged," she told the BBC – adding that she had started preparing evacuation bags amid the "constant aftershocks".

Another resident said aftershocks were still rattling the city hours after the initial tremor.

"People are wary of another earthquake on the way," he said. "The 2016 earthquake earthquake [was] followed by a second days later."

body.zh: 日本西南部城市八代市的仙丹食堂 (Sendan Shokudo) 当天的生意正逐渐接近尾声，突然整个建筑突然摇晃起来。 厨房架子上的所有东西都掉到了地板上；碗和玻璃杯都碎了。 “我很惊讶，也很害怕，”她告诉英国广播公司新闻。 “我立刻钻到了一张桌子底下，但桌子和我一起急剧地向右、向左、向右、向左移动。” 该地区位于活跃的构造断层系统上，对地震并不陌生。 2016年，两次地震造成277人死亡、2800人受伤。 “十年前的最后一次地震与这次完全不同，”她说。 “我以为我会死。” 周二晚间熊本发生里氏 6.8 级地震，造成至少 13 人死亡。 其中三人来自熊本市的永旺购物中心，据信仍有数十人被困。 救援工作正在进行中，但首相高市早苗警告说，紧急服务正在“与时间赛跑”。 地震发生时，距离永旺购物中心仅几百米，Yui* 正坐在蛋糕店的后台办公室里。 “我分不清哪是地震的声音，哪是爆炸的声音，”她告诉英国广播公司。 “我所能做的就是扶住我坐的椅子，剧烈的震动接连而来，”她补充道，看上去仍然处于震惊之中。 “我不知道该有什么感觉，在这种情况下我什至感觉不到害怕。即使现在我也不知道该有什么感觉，也不知道如何解释。” 当局和应急人员迅速动员起来。地震发生后不久，高市派出 4,600 名人员到现场协助恢复工作，并表示各小组将“整夜不知疲倦地工作”，评估和监测受影响地区的损失。 尽管如此，熊本市仍有数万人遭遇停电停水，至少 45 个医疗设施受损。 位于市中心的 17 世纪熊本城的外墙在一阵尘土中倒塌。 19世纪的八代神社的参拜殿彻底倒塌。 当地一位居民米哈尔·波桑 (Michal Posan) 表示，“商店里已经没有水或食物了”。 25 岁的波桑已经在熊本生活了两年，地震发生时他在家中。 她告诉英国广播公司：“我的电视掉落在我身上，镜子被砸碎，周围的道路也被损坏。”她还补充说，在“持续不断的余震”中，她已经开始准备疏散袋。 另一位居民表示，在最初的地震发生几个小时后，余震仍在困扰着这座城市。 “人们对即将发生的另一场地震保持警惕，”他说。 “2016 年地震发生后，第二天又发生了地震。” 专家们也很关心......

reflection.en: In the face of such overwhelming natural disaster, it is natural to feel burdened beyond strength, as if life itself is too much to bear. Yet, even in these moments of profound shock and despair, Yahweh is present, offering a quiet strength to endure.
reflection.zh: 面对如此压倒性的自然灾害，感到力不能胜，甚至觉得生命本身难以承受，这是人之常情。然而，即使在这些极度震惊和绝望的时刻，雅伟依然同在，赐予我们安静的力量去忍耐。

verse.textEn: We were under great pressure, far beyond our ability to endure, so that we despaired of life itself.
verse.textZh: 我们被压太重，力不能胜，甚至连活命的指望都绝了。

title.en: 'No safe options' for thousands sheltering in key Sudan city as RSF fighters advance
title.zh: 随着快速支援部队推进，苏丹关键城市数千名避难者“无安全选择”

summary.en: International leaders have warned that the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) may be preparing to attack a key city in Sudan, raising fears of further atrocities against thousands of civilians sheltering there who have no safe options.
summary.zh: 国际领导人警告称，快速支援部队（RSF）可能正准备袭击苏丹一座重要城市，这引发了人们对数千名在该市避难的平民可能遭受更多暴行的担忧，他们目前没有安全的避难选择。

body.en:
Thousands of people who have poured into the city of el-Obeid hoping to find shelter from Sudan's raging civil war have found themselves under threat again, amid warnings that paramilitary fighters are preparing to descend on the army-controlled city.

Clashes between the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and the military has escalated in the North Kordofan region - a critical target for both sides in the conflict which could open a gateway into contested territory.

Displaced people have flocked to el-Obeid, which remains heavily defended by the Sudanese military, despite ongoing strikes being carried out on the city as paramilitary forces advance. The UN's International Organization for Migration (IOM) said it has become a key refuge for people escaping ongoing violence in the surrounding areas.

Satellite imagery shows the main displacement camp has expanded significantly since March, with aid workers reporting dozens of new arrivals each day.

"Families have run out of safe options to protect themselves," Mohamed Refaat, IOM chief of mission in Sudan, said. "Many have already been displaced before and are once again forced to leave behind their homes, livelihoods and support networks."

The UN and G7 foreign ministers have now issued warnings that the RSF may be preparing to attack the city, raising fears that atrocities akin to those seen during the massacre in el-Fasher could be repeated . Thousands of people were killed in mass executions after the paramilitary overran SAF troops defending the city last October, in one of the worst atrocities since the civil war began in 2023.

Fears of similar reprisals occurring in el-Obeid have grown for weeks and verified footage now shows dozens of heavily armed RSF troops in armoured trucks stationed in Nyala, a key nearby stronghold, vowing to "liberate" the city.

The RSF launched a record number of drone strikes on the city in June, according to the monitoring group Armed Conflict Location and Event Data (Acled). The number of attacks only fell in July because the RSF was responding to Sudanese military attacks elsewhere in Sudan, analysts added.

Satellite images show that despite the strikes, el-Obeid's displacement camp has continued to swell, with hundreds of new tents erected since March. The UN has estimated that more than 83,000 civilians have now fled fighting in other parts of the state and sought shelter in the city.

As the displacement camps have expanded, the conditions in el-Obeid have deteriorated. Last week the UN warned nearly 400,000 people in the city's vicinity are facing food shortages, following a sustained effort by RSF commanders to cut off supply routes into the city for months, creating what one UN official called a "functional siege".

body.zh: 数千人涌入奥贝德市，希望在苏丹激烈的内战中找到庇护所，但他们发现自己再次受到威胁，有警告称，准军事武装分子正准备袭击这座由军队控制的城市。 北科尔多凡地区准军事快速支援部队（RSF）与军方之间的冲突升级，该地区是冲突双方的关键目标，可能打开进入有争议领土的大门。 流离失所者纷纷涌向奥贝德，尽管随着准军事部队的推进，该市仍受到苏丹军队的重兵防守。联合国国际移民组织（IOM）表示，这里已成为逃离周边地区持续暴力的人们的重要避难所。 卫星图像显示，自三月份以来，主要的流离失所者营地已显着扩大，援助人员报告说，每天都有数十名新难民抵达。 国际移民组织驻苏丹代表团团长穆罕默德·雷法特表示：“家庭已经没有安全的选择来保护自己。” “许多人之前已经流离失所，并再次被迫离开家园、生计和支持网络。” 联合国和七国集团外交部长现已发出警告，称无国界部队可能准备袭击该城市，引发人们担心类似法希尔大屠杀期间的暴行可能会重演。去年 10 月，准军事部队碾压了守卫该市的苏丹武装部队，导致数千人被大规模处决，这是自 2023 年内战开始以来最严重的暴行之一。 数周以来，人们对奥贝德发生类似报复的担忧与日俱增，经核实的镜头显示，数十名全副武装的无国界支援部队士兵乘坐装甲车驻扎在附近的一个重要据点尼亚拉，誓言要“解放”这座城市。 根据武装冲突位置和事件数据监测组织 (Acled) 的数据，无国界医生组织 6 月份对该市发动的无人机袭击次数创下了纪录。分析人士补充说，7 月份的袭击次数才有所下降，因为无国界医生组织正在对苏丹其他地方的苏丹军事袭击做出反应。 卫星图像显示，尽管发生了袭击，奥贝德的流离失所者营地仍在不断扩大，自三月份以来已经搭建了数百个新帐篷。联合国估计，目前已有超过 83,000 名平民逃离该州其他地区的战斗，并在该市寻求庇护。 随着流离失所者营地的扩大，奥贝德的条件日益恶化。上周，联合国警告称，无国界医生部队指挥官数月来持续努力切断进入该市的补给路线，造成了一名联合国官员所说的“功能性围困”，该市附近近 40 万人正面临粮食短缺。 此前，当地人曾表示...

Isaiah 58:7 urges us to share with the hungry, bring the homeless into our homes, and not hide ourselves from those in need. In such dire circumstances, the world is called to respond with tangible acts of care and protection for the...
reflection.zh: 苏丹数千人无处可避，这提醒我们雅伟对实际怜悯的呼召。以赛亚书58:7敦促我们与饥饿的人分享食物，将无家可归者带入家中，不向有需要的人隐藏自己。在如此严峻的形势下，世界被呼召以具体的关怀和保护行动来回应那些脆弱的生命。

title.en: 'Israeli settlers laid siege to our home': Inside a Palestinian village under weekly attack
title.zh: “以色列定居者围困我们的家园”：一个每周遭受袭击的巴勒斯坦村庄内部实况

summary.en: A Palestinian home on the outskirts of al-Mughayyir village has become a focal point of conflict, reportedly facing weekly attacks from Israeli settlers. The residents describe living under a constant siege in the occupied West Bank.
summary.zh: 位于穆加耶尔村边缘的一户巴勒斯坦人家，据报道每周都遭到以色列定居者的袭击，已成为被占领的约旦河西岸冲突的前线。居民们形容他们生活在持续的围困之中。

body.en:
The large, bolted gate of the Abu Alia family compound in al-Mughayyir village held firm against the teenage settlers; its thin metal bars ringing with each blow, as they smashed it again and again with their clubs.

One offensive slur - almost identical in both Hebrew and Arabic - delivered with nonchalant contempt by the Israeli boys bashing at the gate; and with fear and frustration by the Palestinian man inches away from them on the other side, filming the encounter on his phone.

This gate, on the edge of al-Mughayyir, has become a weekly frontline in the battle for the occupied West Bank. And this kind of attack by settlers on Palestinian homes, a weekly routine in villages across the territory.

When we arrived in al-Mughayyir that day, the confrontation at the Abu Alia compound had already begun.

The Israeli army and border police were already moving through the streets, and residents were running from their vehicles - soldiers, like settlers, are seen as the enemy here. Some young men rolled rocks into the road to block it, as the sound of gunshots cracked over the village.

On the hill above them, the local mosque was calling on people to help the family trapped by the settlers. But slipping past Israeli soldiers has become a dangerous gamble. Residents, medical workers and journalists have all been shot during Israeli military operations in the West Bank.

This is what passes for a normal weekend now in al-Mughayyir, and in villages across the West Bank, but it rarely breaks beyond the local news.

We spent a week around al-Mughayyir, and its neighbouring village, Khirbet Abu Falah, to see what life was like here for a single community, or a single family.

What we found shows how quickly control of this landscape is changing, and how local attacks by settlers here are the tip of a national project to bring West Bank land under Israeli control.

Since occupying the West Bank during the 1967 Middle East war, Israel has built more than 100 settlements housing more than half a million Jews on land Palestinians want for a future state. Some Israeli settlers have also established hundreds of wildcat outposts - often starting with a single tent or caravan on a hilltop, and often very close to Palestinian homes. Both Israel's official settlements and its outposts are illegal under international law.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has described those carrying out settler attacks as a handful of misguided young people: "150 juvenile delinquents", he's called them, or "70 teenagers from broken homes".

reflection.en: For families enduring relentless pressure and weekly attacks, the experience can feel like an unending siege. Yet, even in the face of sustained hardship, the Scripture reminds us that Yahweh's mercies are new every morning, offering a constant source of hope and strength. This enduring faithfulness can sustain hearts through the longest nights of trial.

title.en: Saudi Arabian forces join US in strikes on Iran-backed militants in Iraq
title.zh: 沙特阿拉伯军队与美国一道打击伊拉克境内伊朗支持的武装分子

summary.en: Saudi Arabian forces have joined the US in conducting military strikes against Iran-backed militants in Iraq. These strikes were carried out in response to recent drone attacks by the militants on US forces and Saudi energy infrastructure.
summary.zh: 沙特阿拉伯军队与美国一道，对伊拉克境内的伊朗支持的武装分子发动了军事打击。此前，这些武装分子曾对美国军队和沙特能源基础设施发动了二十多次无人机袭击。

body.en:
United States and Saudi Arabian warplanes carried out strikes on Wednesday against Iran-backed militants in Iraq who launched more than two dozen drone attacks in recent days, the US military said.

The strikes targeted "Iran-aligned terrorists that the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) directed to attack US forces and Saudi energy infrastructure," US Central Command (CENTCOM) said in a statement.

It further warned that "the IRGC and its terrorist proxies must cease these attacks to avoid further US military response".

The CENTCOM statement did not mention the exact location it said Iran attempted to target.

Saudi Arabia confirmed its involvement in the strikes, with its defence ministry saying it hit "targets belonging to those militias present on Iraqi territory that are linked to attacks on the kingdom's oil facilities".

The strikes came after the ministry said its forces had intercepted drones targeting oil facilities in the east, blaming Iran-backed groups in Iraq.

Saudi Arabia called the previous day for the Iraqi government to prevent attacks from its territory, after which Iraq said it had ordered an investigation.

The IRGC later said they fired several ballistic missiles at a US air base and a US military CENTCOM centre in Jordan, in what they described as a response to US actions against Iranian interests.

US outlet Axios earlier reported, citing a US official, that Iran had launched ballistic missiles towards a US base in Jordan and the missiles were intercepted.

US President Donald Trump, who abruptly called off a two-week bombing campaign on Iran over the weekend, has said there were "good talks" underway with Iran but threatened to restart strikes unless negotiations delivered.

This principle invites us to seek ways that transcend mere reaction, fostering true peace even amidst conflict.

title.en: Japan quake toll rises to 13 as rescuers search for people trapped in collapsed mall
title.zh: 日本地震死亡人数升至13人，救援人员搜寻被困商场人员

summary.en: Rescuers in Japan are searching for people trapped after an earthquake struck, with the death toll rising to 13. The southern prefecture of Kumamoto has a history of devastating earthquakes, including a major one in 2016 that killed hundreds.
summary.zh: 日本救援人员正在搜寻地震中被困人员，死亡人数已升至13人。熊本县南部曾经历多次毁灭性地震，包括2016年造成数百人死亡的大地震。

body.en:
A 7.1-magnitude earthquake killed at least 13 people near the southern Japanese city of Kumamoto, and rescuers are frantically searching for survivors trapped beneath the rubble, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said on Wednesday.

"Even now, there are people waiting to be rescued, and this is a race against time. We will marshal all available resources on the ground to save and rescue as many people as possible," Takaichi told reporters at her office in Tokyo a day after the quake struck, raising the toll from three deaths reported earlier.

The quake knocked out power to thousands of homes and ruptured roads across the region.

Rescuers pulled eight people from the rubble of a partially collapsed shopping mall early on Wednesday. Two women in their 20s were killed as an apparent explosion of unknown origin ripped the mall apart about an hour after the earthquake.

Emergency fire rescue teams, police and army personnel were focusing on areas of the building where calls for help had been received.

Around 20 to 30 mall workers were unaccounted for on Tuesday, public broadcaster NHK said. Seven people are also missing after a chimney collapsed at a Nippon Paper Industries factory, while four others are seriously injured, a local government official said. Hospitals were reported to be treating dozens of patients.

Across the prefecture, which also suffered a deadly earthquake a decade ago, around 260,000 people were instructed to go to evacuation centres, authorities said.

The quake's epicentre was about 20km south of Kumamoto City, central Kyushu's largest city, with a population of around 700,000.

Authorities have warned residents in the areas that felt the biggest tremors to be on alert for further strong quakes for about a week, as well as for the risk of landslides.

With more than 36,000 homes still without power, authorities are worried about the risk of heat stroke as temperatures soar to around 34C on Wednesday.

One hospital in Uki city, near the epicentre, said a power outage caused by the earthquake meant it was unable to function.

"It's become like a field hospital," the head of the administrative department told NHK. Another hospital in the city said it had suspended admissions as it could no longer handle additional emergency cases after accepting 86 injured people following the quake, including three with serious injuries.

Several passengers aboard high-speed trains at the time of the quake were also injured, operators said.

But it was the AEON mall, the largest in the prefecture, that was the most eye-catching disaster.

title.en: 'Not out of danger': Spain's wildfire evacuees return home as France fears flame spread
title.zh: 西班牙野火撤离者返家，法国担忧火势蔓延，“尚未脱离危险”

summary.en: Evacuees in 13 regions of Spain have been cleared to return home following wildfires, while neighboring France remains on high alert due to continued dry, tinderbox conditions and fears of further flame spread.
summary.zh: 西班牙13个地区的撤离人员已获准在森林大火后返回家园，而邻国法国因持续干燥、易燃的条件而保持高度戒备，并担心火势进一步蔓延。

body.en:
Spanish residents forced to flee some of the worst wildfires in living memory began returning to their homes on Wednesday, but thousands more were ordered to leave in France over fears that a looming heatwave would prevent containment of fires that have ripped through the country's southwest.

Swathes of tinder-dry forests, parched land and property have been destroyed west of the Spanish capital, Madrid, and in France's Gironde and Landes regions, forcing tens of thousands to head to safety.

Spain's interior ministry announced the end of evacuation orders for 13 municipalities on Tuesday afternoon local time, in rare good news for locals.

In the evacuated village of Navas del Rey, Reporters from the Agence France-Presse (AFP) news agency saw blackened debris, ash and burnt-out cars.

According to an initial estimate provided to AFP by municipal authorities, around 50 homes were destroyed by the flames and another 50 damaged.

Maria Paz Bolanos, 62, returned with her family to their home and garden in a housing development in the town — and found it only slightly scorched.

"We've been here 50 years," she said. "It must have been grandfather, my father in heaven. He somehow made it so the fire just came in through and stopped right there.

The mayor of nearby Pelayos de la Presa, Antonio Sin, described the scene as "a war zone".

"It has been a horrendous fire, a brutal one — it's a monster that has run over us," he told AFP.

In contrast, Marielle Mourgeon was among 4,000 people forced to cut short holidays in the French seaside village of Lacanau, in the Gironde area near Bordeaux, after camping sites were told to evacuate as a precaution.

"At first I thought my husband was joking, with the blue sky and the fires dying down," she said.

Over the past six days, the largest French wildfire since 1949 has raged west of Bordeaux , forcing more than 220,000 people to flee, destroying 240 houses and prompting questions about emergency preparedness.

Sophie Brocas, the government's top official in Gironde, told reporters the fire had "stabilised... meaning it is not advancing", and authorised nearly 60,000 people evacuated from three villages around the city to return.

South of Lege Cap Ferret on the Atlantic coast, volunteers have been working round the clock to help firefighters restock with water to tackle a wave of fires.

"We pour 8,000 litres on an area, and an hour later it starts up again," said one volunteer, Pierre Marie, after a 12-hour day.

verse.textZh: 就是在患难中也是欢欢喜喜的；因为知道患难生忍耐，忍耐生老练，老练生盼望。

title.en: Fujimori takes charge in Peru amid China, US balancing act
title.zh: 藤森在秘鲁掌权，在中美之间寻求平衡

summary.en: Peru's new president, Keiko Fujimori, has promised more security and investment. Now in office, she'll have to find space for the South American nation amid Washington and Beijing's geopolitical rivalry.
summary.zh: 秘鲁新任总统藤森惠子承诺将加强安全和投资。上任后，她将不得不在华盛顿和北京的地缘政治竞争中为这个南美国家找到自己的定位。

body.en:
Peru's new president, Keiko Fujimori, has promised more security and investment. Now in office, she'll have to find space for the South American nation amid Washington and Beijing's geopolitical rivalry.

Keiko Fujimori's swearing in on Tuesday marked the return of a political movement that had been out of power for more than a quarter century.

Fujimorism, a mix of neoliberalism, populism and strict government policies, characterized the 1990-2000 presidency of her father, the late Alberto Fujimori. Keiko Fujimori is stepping in amid a climate of social polarization, with promises to deliver more security, economic recovery and improvements in the health and education sectors.

But beyond those domestic projects, Fujimori is taking charge at a time of increased strategic importance for Peru . The country has become one of the key battlegrounds in the growing competition between the United States and China for political influence in South America.

Fujimori has already signaled that security will be the top priority for her government.

On the agenda: more video surveillance, a stronger police presence, tougher punishment for crimes and organized gangs, and command and control centers across the country. Part of the crackdown includes the construction of four mega-prisons, like those in El Salvador .

Eliana Carlin, a political science expert at the Pontifical Catholic University of Peru in Lima, is concerned by how Fujimori's plans will affect human rights .

"Behind [these measures] lie strong ideological positions intended to justify making the police and the armed forces solely subject to military jurisdiction," she said.

In addition to a stronger focus on security, Fujimori has said she intends to advance infrastructure projects, attract private investment, build new schools and hospitals and modernize the country with the help of technology and artificial intelligence .

But delivering on these pledges depends largely on whether the government can find the necessary funds. Infrastructure and essential services continue to face significant deficits. Added to that is the surging crime rate and the threat of the strengthening El Nino weather pattern , which could hit Peru with increased drought, extreme heat , flooding and other climate-related disruptions.

Foreign policy is also a major challenge for Fujimori's administration. The opening of the Chancay port and logistics hub has turned Peru into a strategic player in regional trade — and made it a central focus in the geopolitical rivalry between Washington and Beijing.

The estimated $3.5 billion (€3 billion) project is part of China's world-spanning Belt ⁠and Road Initiative . Once fully operational, the port is expected to reduce the shipping time between Peru and China from...
body.zh: 秘鲁新总统藤森庆子承诺提供更多安全和投资。现在就职后，她必须在华盛顿和北京的地缘政治竞争中为这个南美国家找到空间。 藤森惠子周二宣誓就职，标志着一场已经失去权力超过四分之一个世纪的政治运动的回归。 藤森主义是新自由主义、民粹主义和严格政府政策的混合体，是她父亲、已故阿尔贝托·藤森 1990 年至 2000 年总统任期的特征。藤森庆子在社会两极分化的气氛中介入，承诺提供更多安全、经济复苏以及卫生和教育部门的改善。 但除了这些国内项目之外，藤森在秘鲁的战略重要性日益增加之际负责这一项目。该国已成为美国和中国争夺南美政治影响力日益激烈的竞争的关键战场之一。 藤森已经表示，安全将是她的政府的首要任务。 议程包括：更多的视频监控、更强大的警察力量、对犯罪和有组织团伙更严厉的惩罚，以及全国各地的指挥和控制中心。镇压行动的一部分包括建造四座大型监狱，就像萨尔瓦多的监狱一样。 利马秘鲁天主教大学政治学专家埃利安娜·卡林 (Eliana Carlin) 对藤森的计划将如何影响人权表示担忧。 “[这些措施]背后隐藏着强烈的意识形态立场，旨在证明警察和武装部队完全受军事管辖是合理的，”她说。 除了更加关注安全之外，藤森还表示，她打算推进基础设施项目，吸引私人投资，建设新学校和医院，并借助技术和人工智能实现国家现代化。 但兑现这些承诺很大程度上取决于政府能否找到必要的资金。基础设施和基本服务继续面临严重赤字。除此之外，犯罪率飙升以及厄尔尼诺天气模式加强的威胁可能会给秘鲁带来更多的干旱、酷热、洪水和其他与气候相关的破坏。 外交政策也是藤森政府面临的重大挑战。钱凯港口和物流中心的开放使秘鲁成为区域贸易的战略参与者，并使其成为华盛顿和北京之间地缘政治竞争的焦点。 该项目预计耗资 35 亿美元（30 亿欧元），是中国覆盖全球的“一带一路”倡议的一部分。一旦全面投入运营，该港口预计将减少秘鲁和中国之间的运输时间...

reflection.en: As Peru's new president navigates the complex geopolitical landscape between major global powers, the need for wise counsel becomes paramount. For a nation to find stability and safety, its leaders must seek abundant guidance in their decisions. This principle reminds us that no leader can succeed alone, especially when facing intricate international...
reflection.zh: 秘鲁新总统在主要全球大国之间复杂的地理政治格局中航行，对智慧谋略的需求变得至关重要。一个国家若要寻求稳定和安全，其领导人必须在决策中寻求丰富的指导。这一原则提醒我们，没有领导者可以独自成功，尤其是在面对错综复杂的国际挑战时。

verse.textEn: For lack of guidance a nation falls, but victory is won through many advisers.
verse.textZh: 无智谋，民就败落；谋士多，人便安居。

title.en: EU civil protection mechanism: Coordinating Europe's firefighters
title.zh: 欧盟民事保护机制：协调欧洲消防员

summary.en: French President Emmanuel Macron has activated the EU civil protection mechanism to help combat devastating wildfires. The system has shown increasing effectiveness but is projected to reach its operational limits by the summer of 2026.
summary.zh: 法国总统马克龙已启动欧盟民事保护机制，以协助扑灭破坏性野火。该系统已日益高效，但预计将在2026年夏季达到其极限。

body.en:
French President Emmanuel Macron has activated the EU civil protection mechanism to help combat devastating wildfires. The system has become increasingly effective, yet it will reach its limits in the summer of 2026.

France is quite well-prepared for wildfires. The government operates 12 Canadair water bombers and eight Dash firefighting aircraft. In addition, leased aircraft and helicopters are being used.

However, the fleet is currently needed simultaneously across many parts of the country. A drought has been intensifying for weeks, and several heat waves with temperatures sometimes exceeding 40 degrees Celsius (104 Fahrenheit) have left the vegetation extremely parched. The devastating wildfire near Bordeaux on the Atlantic coast has already engulfed more than 42,000 hectares of forest and vegetation.

At the same time, fires and follow-up extinguishing efforts in southern and southeastern France  are tying up additional emergency personnel. In many places, firefighters are battling the flames in an exhausting, round-the-clock effort. However, strong winds are fanning the fire fronts, making them almost unstoppable, and more than 220,000 people have had to leave their homes and vacation homes so far.

The gravity of the situation is also underscored by the fact that the French government has deployed an A400M military transport aircraft equipped for aerial firefighting for the first time. The A400M can drop around 20 metric tons of fire retardant, more than three times as much as a Canadair.

Nevertheless, the situation is currently so dire that President Emmanuel Macron also activated the EU civil protection mechanism (CPM) and requested assistance from other European countries.

To activate the CPM, a country reports its needs to the European Union's emergency response coordination centre, ERCC, in Brussels . ERCC experts assess which of the 37 participating countries can provide assistance.

Initial assistance for France was mobilized within a few hours and has since been significantly expanded. Firefighting aircraft and helicopters from Portugal , Croatia , the Czech Republic , Germany , Turkey , Sweden  and Slovakia  are supporting France, primarily in the greater Bordeaux area.

At the same time, however, the EU also dispatched six additional firefighting aircraft from Greece , Turkey and Italy to Spain . This means that 13 of the 22 firefighting aircraft available for this summer have already been mobilized for these two countries. The figures also demonstrate how quickly the European reserve can be drawn upon when multiple large-scale wildfires occur simultaneously. According to the European Commission , the resources currently available are therefore likely insufficient to keep pace with the scale of the...
body.zh: 法国总统马克龙启动了欧盟民事保护机制，以帮助扑灭毁灭性的野火。该系统已经变得越来越有效，但将在 2026 年夏季达到极限。 法国已经为野火做好了充分的准备。政府运营 12 架加拿大航空水轰炸机和 8 架 Dash 消防机。此外，还使用租赁的飞机和直升机。 然而，目前全国许多地区都同时需要这支车队。几周来干旱一直在加剧，几次热浪的温度有时超过 40 摄氏度（104 华氏度），导致植被极度干燥。大西洋沿岸波尔多附近的毁灭性野火已经吞噬了超过 42,000 公顷的森林和植被。 与此同时，法国南部和东南部的火灾和后续灭火工作需要更多的应急人员。 在许多地方，消防员正在日以继夜地与大火奋力搏斗。然而，强风助长了火势，几乎势不可挡，迄今为止已有超过 22 万人不得不离开家园和度假屋。 法国政府首次部署配备空中消防装备的A400M军用运输机，也凸显了事态的严重性。 A400M 可投放约 20 吨阻燃剂，是加拿大航空飞机的三倍多。 尽管如此，目前形势十分严峻，马克龙总统也启动了欧盟民事保护机制（CPM），并向欧洲其他国家请求援助。 为了启动 CPM，一个国家需要向位于布鲁塞尔的欧盟应急响应协调中心 ERCC 报告其需求。 ERCC 专家评估 37 个参与国中哪些国家可以提供援助。 对法国的初步援助在几个小时内就动员起来，此后大幅扩大了援助范围。来自葡萄牙、克罗地亚、捷克共和国、德国、土耳其、瑞典和斯洛伐克的消防飞机和直升机正在为法国提供支持，主要是在大波尔多地区。 不过与此同时，欧盟还从希腊、土耳其和意大利增派了六架消防机前往西班牙。这意味着今年夏天可用的 22 架消防飞机中的 13 架已经为这两个国家调动。这些数字还表明，当多场大规模野火同时发生时，可以多快地动用欧洲储备。据欧盟委员会称，目前可用的资源可能不足以跟上......的规模。

reflection.en: As Europe coordinates efforts against devastating wildfires, the news that current systems will reach their limits by 2026 highlights the need for foresight and wise planning. In facing complex challenges like these, we are reminded to seek wisdom from Yahweh, who generously provides it to all who ask. This divine guidance can illuminate paths forward when...
reflection.zh: 欧洲协调应对破坏性野火之际，现有系统预计将在2026年达到极限的消息，凸显了远见和明智规划的必要性。面对此类复杂挑战，我们被提醒要向雅伟寻求智慧，祂会慷慨地赐予所有求问的人。当人类的解决方案似乎力不从心或接近极限时，这种神圣的指引能够照亮前进的道路。

verse.textEn: If any of you lacks wisdom, you should ask God, who gives generously to all without finding fault.
verse.textZh: 你们中间若有缺少智慧的，应当求那厚赐与众人、也不斥责人的神，主就必赐给他。

title.en: Poland: Top court rejects recognizing EU same-sex marriages
title.zh: 波兰：最高法院拒绝承认欧盟同性婚姻

summary.en: Poland's constitutional court has rejected the recognition of same-sex marriages performed in other EU member states. This decision goes against a ruling from the EU's highest court and may lead to a legal conflict.
summary.zh: 波兰宪法法院驳回了承认在其他欧盟成员国缔结的同性婚姻的计划。这一裁决违背了欧盟最高法院的命令，可能引发一场法律冲突。

body.zh: 波兰宪法法院推翻了承认其他欧盟成员国同性婚姻的计划。这违反了欧盟最高法院的命令，并可能在此事上引发冲突。 波兰最高法院宪法法庭周二推翻了一项法律，该法律本应在法律上承认在其他欧盟成员国结婚并随后移居波兰的同性配偶。 华沙政府一直在采取行动，以适应欧盟法院的一项裁决，该裁决称，天​​主教徒占多数的波兰不允许国内同性婚姻，因此必须至少承认在欧盟其他地方签订的工会。 这项一致裁决可能会引发波兰最高法院与 27 个成员国联盟之间的权力斗争。 法院在周二的一份声明中表示，该判决是一致的、最终的，欧盟同性婚姻不能按照之前的计划复制到该国的民事登记处。 它表示，“准备和签发有关不构成男女之间婚姻的国外合同的经核证副本”的计划“不符合波兰共和国宪法第92条第1款以及第18条”。 宪法第18条规定：“婚姻是一男一女的结合，以及家庭、母亲和父母身份，应置于波兰共和国的保护和照顾之下。” 换句话说，它既指定婚姻本质上是异性恋，又是波兰管辖范围的一部分。 第九十二条第一项同时规定，规章应由“宪法规定的机关”制定。 法院没有在简短的声明中详细说明其推理，但这似乎表明法官认为欧洲法院的命令侵犯了波兰制定家庭和婚姻政策的权力。 欧盟法院 2025 年 11 月的裁决并未要求波兰将同性婚姻合法化，甚至也没有要求其在法律上承认同性配偶。 然而，它确实要求，在欧盟其他地方合法结婚，然后在波兰等另一个国家行使“迁徙和居住自由”的同性伴侣，如果这是确保该国婚姻状况的利益和保障的唯一途径，则应将其婚姻状况复制到民事登记册中。 该案件由两名男子发起，一名波兰公民，一名德国-波兰双重国籍，他们于 2018 年在德国居住期间合法结婚，并于次年移居波兰。 波兰最高行政法院...

As societies navigate these complex issues, the enduring biblical perspective offers a...

title.en: Could US airstrikes stop insurgency in Mali?
title.zh: 美国空袭能否阻止马里叛乱？

summary.en: US President Donald Trump is reportedly considering airstrikes against the Al-Qaeda-linked JNIM in Mali. Analysts suggest that while such attacks might weaken the jihadist group, they would not resolve the underlying core issues of the conflict.
summary.zh: 据多方报道，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普正在考虑对马里与基地组织有关联的JNIM发动空袭。分析人士指出，此类袭击或许能削弱圣战分子，但无法解决核心问题。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump is considering airstrikes against the Al-Qaeda-linked JNIM in Mali, according to multiple reports. Analysts say such attacks might weaken the jihadists but would not address the core issues.

For years, Mali has struggled to contain a growing jihadist insurgency , particularly in the country's northern region. Following the withdrawal of French troops and despite the authorities' close cooperation with Russia , the al-Qaeda-linked Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM) continues to expand its influence. Now, a new actor could enter the conflict: the United States (US) .

Founded in 2017, JNIM unites several Islamist groups under the banner of al-Qaeda . Over the past years, the organization has developed into the most powerful jihadist force in the Sahel . Its objective is the establishment of an Islamist order and the displacement of state structures as well as Western influence.

"We are no longer talking about a group that only carries out isolated attacks," explains Tobias Rüttershof, head of the Sahel Program of the Konrad Adenauer Foundation (KAS), which is affiliated with Germany's CDU party and has an office in Mali, in an interview with DW. "In many regions, JNIM effectively controls the security situation, collects taxes, mediates local conflicts and in some areas is more present than the Malian state." 

According to the US National Counterterrorism Center, JNIM was responsible for more than 1,200 deaths in 2025, making it the second-deadliest terrorist organization in the world. Particularly concerning is the group's geographic expansion: JNIM is now active not only in Burkina Faso and Niger , but increasingly in the coastal states of West Africa. 

The US government is divided over the question of direct military strikes. Supporters such as Sebastian Gorka, senior director for counterterrorism at the National Security Council, argue that JNIM is one of the world's most dangerous jihadist organizations and that its advance must be halted.

Russia's security strategy in Mali has so far failed to deliver results, according to Rüttershof. 

"After the withdrawal of French forces, the UN mission MINUSMA , and European training missions, Mali's military government argued that  Russia could stabilize the security situation more effectively," Gorka told DW. "That expectation has not been fulfilled so far. On the contrary, JNIM appears stronger today than it was several years ago."

Following military coups in 2020 and 2021, Bamako increasingly distanced itself from Western partners and expanded cooperation with Russia.

The Malian government has responded cautiously to reports of possible US airstrikes.

title.en: Trump administration bans new Chinese humanoid robots

summary.en: The United States has imposed a ban on new Chinese humanoid robots, intensifying the ongoing competition between the two nations to achieve global leadership in the fields of robotics and artificial intelligence.
summary.zh: 美国已禁止新的中国类人机器人，这加剧了两国在机器人和人工智能领域争夺全球领导地位的竞争。

body.en:
The Trump administration on Tuesday announced a ban on new foreign-made humanoid robot imports to the US over "unacceptable risks" to America's national security.

The move applies to advanced robots - including humanoid and four-legged machines. Many of them are made in China, which is competing with the US to develop robotics and artificial intelligence (AI).

The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) also banned imports of power inverters - devices used in data centres and solar panels - which it said could also pose a risk to the US economy.

The Chinese embassy in Washington said Beijing has long opposed the US' "politicising" of trade issues and sanctions based on "groundless pretexts".

FCC chairman Brendan Carr said the agency was doing its part "to secure America's critical supply chains".

The FCC has added the items to its Covered List - a register of goods and services that are deemed a risk to US national security.

The ban applies to new foreign-produced advanced robotic devices and power inverters and does not prevent the sale or import of any existing models that had been previously authorised by the FCC.

The FCC cited concerns that the use of foreign-made inverters could allow overseas firms to turn them off, steal data, facilitate remote access and surveillance by "foreign government actors, or be otherwise exploited through a cyberattack".

It added that the use of robots made outside the US could allow "malign actors to surveil Americans, enhance the capabilities of foreign intelligence services, or to remotely commandeer the robots".

The Chinese embassy in Washington also said Beijing will "take all necessary measures" in response to any moves that harm its interests, urging all countries to work together to develop AI "for the positive and for good".

It called on the US to "abandon its hegemonic mindset, and stop smearing Chinese companies and threatening them with sanctions".

The BBC has contacted major Chinese robot manufacturers Unitree, UBTech and AgiBot for comment.

China's exports have come under intense scrutiny by the US as the Trump administration attempts to address trade imbalances with the world's second largest economy.

Despite being the world's biggest exporter of electric vehicles, China has been effectively shut out of the American market by a steep tariff.

Washington has also blocked the sale of cutting-edge US semiconductors to China in a bid to protect national security, slow Beijing's military modernisation and maintain America's lead in AI.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has also warned that Chinese AI firms could face sanctions over allegations that they have stolen American intellectual property .

In response the Chinese government has said its country's development of AI was "the result...

summary.en: A new report indicates that China's strategic influence in the Pacific region, which was once significant, has recently diminished. This shift is noted amidst a broader competition for influence involving countries like Australia.

body.en:
Australia has continued to outrank China as the Pacific's biggest source of development aid, contributing a third of loans and infrastructure investment to the region, according to a new report.

Looking at development projects across the Pacific between 2008 and 2024, the Lowy Institute report found that, after years of decline, aid to the region increased by 10 per cent in 2024.

Total development aid stood at US$4.1 billion ($5.85 billion) in that year, but the report's authors estimate that would drop to US$3.8 billion ($5.42 billion) in yet-to-be-released 2025 figures.

With China now shifting strategy from big debt-fuelled loans to smaller strategic aid, and amid major economic shocks in the Pacific, the contest for regional influence is coming under greater strain.

Australia was the Pacific's biggest donor in 2024, giving $2.14 billion in aid, which made up 37 per cent of all finance to the region in that year.

A total of $6 billion in financing was dispensed from New Zealand, China, and regional development banks.

Australia has also inked $3.4 billion in loan deals, ending China's reign as the region's leading lender.

"That's a product of many years of Australia pushing into these spaces, but it's meant that what was once a real foothold for China in the region has been narrowed," the report's lead author Riley Duke told SBS News.

"Australia is consistently providing the most grant financing to the region, and that picture hasn't really changed."

The report, released on Tuesday, says demand for Chinese loans has dropped since 2019 due to concerns about servicing the debt, more competition between lenders and Chinese banks' capital availability.

Australia is also a major financier of climate change mitigation projects in the Pacific, including a solar and battery storage facility for Palau to help generate 20 per cent of its electricity, and Tonga's Renewable Energy Stabilisation Package.

The fruits of those efforts have paid off for Australia, with a flurry of regional security deals announced in recent months, including with Fiji, Vanuatu , Papua New Guinea and Tuvalu.

"They are a clear marker of Australia establishing itself as the lead partner to the region," Duke said.

"Those deals ... take a long time to progress. They're complicated, but they reflect Australia establishing itself as an inalienably important partner to Pacific countries."

Developing Pacific Island nations have been hit hard by multiple shocks, including the COVID-19 pandemic and more recently, fuel supply shortages caused by the United States-Israeli war on Iran.

summary.en: Activists from Hong Kong, including former legislator Nathan Law, are facing unexpected challenges with UK immigration despite promises of protection. Concerns are rising that their safety might be compromised to foster better diplomatic relations with China.
summary.zh: 包括前立法会议员罗冠聪在内的香港活动人士，尽管英国曾承诺提供保护，但在英国移民方面却面临意想不到的困难。人们担心，他们的安全可能被牺牲，以换取与中国更友好的外交关系。

body.en: Activists under threat from Beijing are facing strange difficulties with UK immigration. Their safety must not be traded for warmer relations with China Nathan Law is a pro-democracy activist and former legislator from Hong Kong. He is currently a political refugee in the UK As authoritarian countries such as Russia, China and Iran are more active in engaging in long-arm strategies to silence their critics in the UK, transnational repression is garnering more attention. It is right that the Metropolitan police and other British law enforcement agencies have specific units and mechanisms to counter it. But it takes more than just confronting this long-distance repression to make political dissidents of these authoritarian countries feel safe in the UK, and the UK government is not living up to expectations. The threat is real. Members of the Hongkonger community have received threats from the Chinese regime – some have had threatening letters, some people were deepfaked into sexual content, some even had families questioned and arrested back home. With the level of this targeting linked to the deterioration of Hong Kong politics, many have utilised the humanitarian pathway enabled by the previous government to relocate. Continue reading...
body.zh: 受到北京威胁的活动人士在英国移民问题上面临着奇怪的困难。不能用他们的安全来换取与中国关系的缓和。罗冠聪是一位民主活动人士，也是香港前立法会议员。他目前是英国的政治难民。随着俄罗斯、中国和伊朗等独裁国家更加积极地采取长臂战略来压制英国的批评者，跨国镇压正在引起更多关注。伦敦警察厅和其他英国执法机构确实有专门的单位和机制来应对。但要让这些独裁国家的政治异见人士在英国感到安全，仅仅面对这种远程镇压是不够的，而英国政府并没有达到人们的期望。威胁是真实的。香港人社区的成员受到了来自中国政权的威胁——有些人收到了恐吓信，有些人被深度伪造色情内容，有些人甚至在国内遭到盘问和逮捕。由于这种目标的程度与香港政治的恶化有关，许多人利用前任政府允许的人道主义途径搬迁。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This situation reminds us of the biblical call to treat foreigners residing among us with the same care and respect as our own citizens. Yahweh's command to love the stranger, remembering our own vulnerability, challenges nations to uphold their commitments to those seeking refuge. It urges us to prioritize human dignity over political expediency.
reflection.zh: 这种情况提醒我们，圣经呼吁我们以对待本国公民的同样关怀和尊重来对待居住在我们中间的外国人。雅伟命令我们要爱寄居的，并记住我们自己也曾是寄居的，这挑战着各国要信守对寻求庇护者的承诺，敦促我们将人的尊严置于政治权宜之上。

verse.textEn: When a foreigner resides among you in your land, do not mistreat them. The foreigner residing among you must be treated as your native-born. Love them as yourself, for you were foreigners in Egypt.
verse.textZh: 若有外人在你们国中和你同居，就不可欺负他。和你们同居的外人，你们要看他如本地人一样，并要爱他如己，因为你们在埃及地也作过寄居的。

title.en: ‘We have lost everything’: extreme rainfall across Asia brings flash floods and typhoons
title.zh: “我们失去了一切”：亚洲极端降雨引发山洪和台风

summary.en: Extreme rainfall across Asia has led to widespread flash floods and typhoons, causing immense devastation from Afghanistan to Taiwan. The unprecedented deluge highlights the severe impact of climate breakdown, with one construction worker describing 10 days and nights of non-stop rain and the loss of everything.
summary.zh: 亚洲各地遭遇极端降雨，引发大范围山洪和台风，从阿富汗到台湾都遭受了巨大破坏。这场前所未有的洪灾凸显了气候崩溃的毁灭性影响，一名建筑工人描述了连续十天十夜的降雨，以及他们失去了一切的困境。

body.en: From Afghanistan to Taiwan, unprecedented deluge highlights devastating impact of climate breakdown “It rained for 10 days and 10 nights, non-stop – I’d never seen anything like it,” says Anar Gul, a construction worker who lives in the remote district of Dur Baba in eastern Afghanistan. The houses in his village are built from stone and mud, which makes them extremely vulnerable to heavy rains. After days of rain, Gul’s kitchen collapsed and his neighbour, Sayed Afsar Sadat, saw a large part of his house completely destroyed. “Rains like this are coming heavier and earlier each year,” says Sadat. “They are destroying the roads and washing away our crops. It’s impacting us directly.” Continue reading...
body.zh: 从阿富汗到台湾，史无前例的洪水突显了气候崩溃的破坏性影响。居住在阿富汗东部杜巴巴偏远地区的建筑工人阿纳尔·古尔 (Anar Gul) 说：“这场雨持续了 10 天 10 夜，不间断，我从来没有见过这样的情况。”他村里的房子都是用石头和泥土建造的，这使得它们极易受到大雨的影响。经过几天的降雨，古尔的厨房倒塌了，他的邻居赛义德·阿夫萨·萨达特 (Sayed Afsar Sadat) 看到他的房子的很大一部分完全被毁。 “像这样的降雨每年都来得更大、更早，”萨达特说。 “他们毁坏了道路，冲走了我们的庄稼。这直接影响着我们。”继续阅读...

title.en: US-China AI rivalry heats up as Chinese models gain ground
title.zh: 中美人工智能竞争加剧，中国模型迎头赶上

summary.en: China's AI platforms are rapidly advancing, narrowing the gap with US technology. This progress has led to renewed threats from the Trump administration, alongside accusations of intellectual property theft, raising concerns about escalating tensions between the two nations.
summary.zh: 中国的人工智能平台正迅速缩小与美国同行的差距。这一进展引发了特朗普政府新的威胁，并伴随着知识产权盗窃的指控，令人担忧两国之间的紧张关系可能升级。

body.en:
China's AI platforms are rapidly closing the gap with their US counterparts, prompting fresh threats from the Trump administration. With accusations of intellectual property theft, could tensions boil over?

In what seems like the blink of an eye,  China has gone from being up to five years behind the United States in top-tier artificial intelligence (AI) to lagging by just a few months.

While US players, including Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's ChatGPT , have spent hundreds of billions of dollars to push the frontier of AI, China has pursued a very different path .

Faced with US curbs on high-end chips that help AI to do its most advanced thinking, Chinese tech firms have prioritized dozens of open-source AI models built on "good enough"  technology .

These platforms, including DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen and Xiaomi's MiMo, are now widely deployed across Chinese businesses, government services and consumer devices.

In the latest sign of the gap closing, Chinese startup Moonshot AI last week unveiled Kimi K3, a model that rivals one of the most advanced AI models — Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 — on key benchmarks.

In some tests, Kimi K3 matches or even surpasses Claude with far less computing power and at a fraction of the cost. 

Global technology specialist Alvin W. Graylin thinks Kimi K3's arrival turns high-end AI from an expensive luxury into something practical and affordable.

"For 98% of customers, the 1 to 2% difference [in knowledge] isn't worth paying 10 to 20 times more."

China's latest advance has already drawn a strong reaction from Washington, with US President Donald Trump now threatening to block US access to Chinese AI models.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, meanwhile, warned earlier this week that the US could sanction Chinese models over alleged intellectual property (IP) theft.

Anthropic  and OpenAI have accused Chinese labs of using their models to train their own systems, a process known as distilling.

While distilling is a common practice by AI labs worldwide to a limited extent, the companies say their models have been bombarded with queries to harvest advanced reasoning. The White House warned in April that China was doing it on an "industrial scale."

Beijing has hit back, rejecting the accusations as baseless and calling US threats of sanctions and model bans "technological bullying" to contain China's rise.

Giulia Neaher, a research analyst at the Strategic Foresight Hub at the Washington-based Stimson Center think tank, downplayed the role of distilling in Kimi's progress.

body.zh: 中国的人工智能平台正在迅速缩小与美国同行的差距，引发了特朗普政府的新威胁。随着知识产权盗窃的指控，紧张局势会升级吗？ 似乎一眨眼的功夫，中国在顶级人工智能 (AI) 领域就从落后美国五年变为仅落后几个月。 尽管包括 Anthropic 的 Claude 和 OpenAI 的 ChatGPT 在内的美国企业已经花费了数千亿美元来推动人工智能的前沿发展，但中国却走了一条截然不同的道路。 面对美国对帮助人工智能实现最先进思维的高端芯片的限制，中国科技公司优先考虑了数十种基于“足够好”技术的开源人工智能模型。 这些平台，包括 DeepSeek、阿里巴巴的 Qwen 和小米的 MiMo，现已广泛部署在中国企业、政府服务和消费设备中。 作为缩小差距的最新迹象，中国初创公司 Moonshot AI 上周推出了 Kimi K3，该模型在关键基准测试上可与最先进的人工智能模型之一——Anthropic 的 Claude Fable 5 相媲美。 在某些测试中，Kimi K3 可以与 Claude 相媲美甚至超过 Claude，但其计算能力却要低得多，而成本却只是 Claude 的一小部分。 全球技术专家 Alvin W. body.en:
Petrol is back above $2 a litre and diesel prices have hit $2.40 in some cities as fuel costs race upwards.

Oil prices have steadily risen since the US resumed strikes on Iran, with Brent crude up from about US$70 on 2 July to US$87 today, while the Australian government reduced its fuel excise discount by 16 cents a litre.

Melbourne is facing diesel prices of $2.40 a litre today, up 66 cents from their June low of 173.9c/L, according to Motormouth. Canberra is at 238c/L, Brisbane is at 234.4, Adelaide at 233.7, Sydney 232.8, and 226.4 in Perth.

Unleaded petrol prices have risen to 204.1 cents a litre in Canberra. They’re at 195.6c/L in Melbourne, 195.2 in Brisbane, 192.6 in Adelaide and 191.1, in Sydney – the latter up from its June low of 152.2. body.en:
Treasurer Jim Chalmers has confirmed the fuel excise discount will end on Sunday 2 August, ending weeks of uncertainty over whether the discount would be extended for a second time.

"It was never the government's intention for [the discount] to be permanent," Chalmers said on Wednesday.

The initial discount of 32c per litre ended in June, after which the government extended the fuel excise cut at a reduced rate of 16c per litre.

"We began to taper that off at the start of the month, deliberately, so that we could provide a bit more cost of living help," Chalmers said.

While the NRMA does expect a modest rise in petrol prices from Monday, the roadside assistance and travel organisation doesn't expect costs to skyrocket.

"Our message to the public is: We know fuel prices are going to go up on Monday and beyond. We don't know by how much," NRMA spokesperson Peter Khoury told SBS News.

"We would expect average prices to go up a few cents per litre ... but it really depends on the service station."

The announcement ended weeks of uncertainty over whether the government would extend the fuel excise discount after Iran resumed its blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, sending global oil markets into shock for the second time since the US-Israeli attacks on the Islamic Republic in February.

Khoury said global oil markets were already responding to news on Monday that both sides had halted bombing , with benchmark unleaded prices dropping.

If the relative calm continues, Khoury said it will "definitely negate the increases we're going to get from the tax being reintroduced".

"We've seen a lot of restraint from the oil companies in the past few weeks," he said, adding that if global oil prices continued to fall it would "cushion the blow" of upcoming price rises in Australia.

Khoury said that price rises caused by the end of the fuel excise discount wouldn't happen overnight.

"Not every service station is going to put their price up by 17 cents a litre. In fact, almost none will. So please don't go out and panic buy."

Khoury told SBS News that, by the time the discount expires, it's likely the increase will be closer to 17 cents rather than the extended excise reduction rate of 16 cents.

"We think it's going to be another cent because of the inflation adjustment, which also just happens to land on the same day [Monday] they do that twice a year."

Just how much cost will be passed on to the consumer depends on individual service stations, Khoury added.

"We don't want people to panic because some service stations will go up on Monday and others won't; it really depends on when they sell their stock."

summary.en: A test flight successfully completed a 24-hour non-stop journey, marking a significant milestone in long-haul air travel. This achievement prompts questions about the future of traditional stopovers.
summary.zh: 一架测试航班成功完成了24小时不间断飞行，标志着长途航空旅行的一个重要里程碑。这一成就引发了人们对传统中途停留未来走向的思考。

body.en:
A record-breaking test flight lasting more than 24 hours has touched down in France from Melbourne — and experts say Australia could be leading the world on the new technology use.

Qantas' specially adapted Airbus A350-1000ULR landed in France on Tuesday after a marathon 24 hours and 24 minutes in the air, covering 23,057km without stopping — the longest direct flight ever attempted by a commercial aircraft.

The flight is part of a two-month test campaign as part of Qantas' Project Sunrise, which aims to launch the world's longest commercial passenger flight and reshape long-haul travel by offering direct flights from Australia's east coast to London and New York.

The previous record belonged to a Boeing 777-200LR, which flew 21,601.7km from Hong Kong to London in 22 hours and 42 minutes back in 2005.

Qantas has ordered 12 of the modified A350 aircraft, each fitted with an extra 20,000-litre fuel tank and configured to seat 238 passengers.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The first is due for delivery in April 2027, with daily non-stop flights between Sydney and London planned from October that year — turning what was once a five-day journey in 1947 on the old 'Kangaroo Route' into a single hop of 19 to 21 hours, depending on winds and routing.

The airline has said a Sydney-New York route will follow shortly after the launch of the London route.

The test flight's success has cast eyes towards the future of air travel, with some wondering whether stopovers in Singapore, Dubai or Los Angeles may be a thing of the past.

Justin Brownjohn from RMIT University's Aviation Academy says non-stop routes will keep becoming more viable as aircraft range improves and fuel use falls — but that doesn't make them a replacement for one-stop flying.

"Airlines have historically competed on network and frequency, but Project Sunrise competes on time," he said.

"Cutting up to four hours off the journey from Sydney to London and removing the connection entirely is a different product, not an improved version of the existing one.

Brownjohn expects the strongest demand for the ultra-long-haul services to come from business and premium leisure travellers willing to pay more for the time saved — and says the wider effect may be felt most by the Middle Eastern and Asian hub airports that have built their business models around the layover.

Spending over 20 hours in the air also raises real questions about passenger wellbeing.

"Twenty hours is not a longer flight, it is a different physiological event," Brownjohn said. "On this flight comfort has stopped being a luxury feature and become the thing being sold."

summary.en: ASIC said banks consistently failed to deliver promises on offset account savings. Here's how to tell if you've been impacted.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Australians have lost millions of dollars to offset account errors, according to a review by the Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC).

The corporate regulator analysed the offset practices of eight banks , which it said represent more than 70 per cent of Australia's $2.5 trillion home loan market.

It found weaknesses in how all banks established, monitored and managed offset accounts.

Reports to ASIC between September 2023 and August 2025 showed that banks paid over $55 million in customer compensation for offset account failures .

In some cases, customers were repaid over $17,000 due to system limitations or administrative errors.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Offset accounts operate like everyday transaction accounts, which can be used to deposit and withdraw money. But they're often marketed as a simple way to reduce home loan interest.

That's because money held in an offset account also reduces the outstanding amount owed on a home loan, which is used to calculate the interest paid on that loan.

If a person has $50,000 in their offset account and a $750,000 loan, they will only be charged interest on $700,000.

Sally Tindall, director of data insights at Canstar, said offset accounts are a popular choice for many Australian mortgage holders .

"For many customers, it's one of the most powerful tools borrowers have to reduce the amount of interest they pay on their mortgage — but only if it's working as intended."

However, offset accounts are often associated with higher interest rates, additional account fees or a combination of both.

ASIC encouraged Australians to check whether their offset account was actually set up following their initial request.

Information about offset accounts should be available via a bank's mobile app, online banking or bank statements.

Some bank sites have mortgage offset pages which outline whether a person is eligible for an offset and how to find their account number.

ASIC's report also warned that refinancing or switching home loan products could break the link between an offset account and a person's mortgage.

In just over a month, a customer paid more than $3,500 in additional interest because their offset account was not linked, ASIC found.

Tindall said: "When you've spent years building up savings in your offset, the last thing you want is for those dollars to be sitting in an account that's not actually reducing your interest bill."

"But don't stop there, do some quick maths to make sure the interest you're being charged is on the amount you actually owe, factoring in the offset balance."

body.en:
Victoria's new premier, Ben Carroll , has four months to claw back support for Labor ahead of the state election on 28 November.

"I will do things differently, because different times require a new approach," he told reporters on Tuesday.

He replaces former premier Jacinta Allan, once the youngest female parliamentarian when she was first elected at age 25, who took on the role of premier in 2023 following Daniel Andrews' resignation .

But Allan's reign as premier saw her net approval ratings plummet in recent months, as she faced mounting criticism over Labor's infrastructure spending and its response to alleged corruption in the construction industry.

An opinion poll conducted by Resolve indicated 43 per cent of Victorians prefer Liberal leader Jess Wilson for state premier, compared with 24 per cent who favour Allan.

Another poll, from RedBridge in July, put the once-popular Labor Party's primary vote at 26 per cent, behind One Nation's 27 per cent.

Ben Carroll's first act as premier was to announce a royal commission into the construction sector, which had been plagued by years of corruption scandals centred on the $109 billion 'Big Build' infrastructure program.

"In my government, integrity will not be optional," Carroll said in his first speech to the press on Tuesday afternoon.

The commission will focus on the Construction, Forestry and Maritime Employees Union (CFMEU), first alleged by the Nine Network in 2024 to have worked with crime organisations to profit from Big Build contracts.

According to the government's website, Big Build has delivered 130 infrastructure projects since 2015 at a cost of around $109 billion, including the controversial Suburban Rail Loop .

In February, an investigation commissioned by the CFMEU estimated Victorian taxpayers had lost $15 billion to organised crime, an untested figure which was disputed by Allan and the state's attorney-general at the time.

The same month, Victorian Liberals and Nationals pledged support for a royal commission.

Allan, who had referred Big Build to the state's anti-corruption watchdog in 2024, resisted calls for a royal commission despite her approval ratings plummeting amid perceived inaction over Big Build corruption.

One Resolve poll, published by Nine in July, had Allan's approval rating at -36 per cent.

As pressure mounted, Allan acknowledged and apologised for criminal conduct on Big Build in an op-ed in The Age in early July.

title.en: The new plan to prevent data centres from driving power prices up
title.zh: 防止数据中心推高电价的新计划

summary.en: Data centres would be forced to invest in additional renewable energy infrastructure in a bid to keep power prices down.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及真理、分辨与诚实。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Large-scale data centres will be forced to invest in additional renewable energy to fuel their operations and avoid causing power price hikes in regulations agreed to by all but two states and territories.

The Energy and Climate Change Ministerial Council revealed its plans late on Tuesday after meeting to discuss advice on the issue from the Australian Energy Market Commission.

Climate groups welcomed the announcement and boost for renewable energy, but an organisation representing data centre operators warned the policy could be counterproductive if designed without their input.

The changes come weeks after Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced plans to require data centres to be powered by clean energy projects under a shake-up of artificial intelligence rules , and after a NSW data centre inquiry heard similar calls for action.

The council, which includes energy ministers from the federal government and all state and territory governments, met virtually to discuss data centre energy proposals after flagging the issue in May.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

All ministers except those from Queensland and the Northern Territory agreed to pursue regulations that would "mandate that data centres offset their electricity demand by investing in additional renewable generation", the meeting communique said.

Renewable energy would need to be generated near the data centre unless local authorities opted out of the requirement, and the rules would be set at a national level, although states and territories could add additional requirements.

Changes to national rules would be considered in September, including reforms to the way data centres reported energy use.

The Climate Council called the proposed changes encouraging, although chief executive Amanda McKenzie said the rules should give data centre operators strict deadlines.

Governments from all Australian states and territories should also support the changes, she said, to avoid penalising some consumers with rising power bills.

"Unless these hold-out governments get on board, Queenslanders and Territorians will be left paying higher power bills, and we will all pay the price of higher climate pollution," she said.

But introducing a blanket rule for data centres' energy use could be ineffective if it was not designed with industry input, Data Centres Australia chief executive Belinda Dennett said.

body.en:
Offset accounts are often marketed as a simple way to reduce home loan interest, but a report by the Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) has found that some banks fail to deliver on that promise.

ASIC, Australia's financial services and consumer credit regulator, reviewed the offset practices of eight banks, which together represent more than 70 per cent of Australia's approximately $2.5 trillion home loan market .

It found that, while practices varied across these financial institutions — AMP, ANZ, CommBank, Great Southern Bank, HSBC Australia, ING, Macquarie Bank and Westpac — there were weaknesses in how they established, monitored and managed offset accounts.

It identified two cases where customers unknowingly paid more than $17,000 extra interest on their home loan because the bank did not make clear that offset accounts had to be re-linked after refinancing.

In another circumstance, a customer paid over $3,500 in additional interest over about a month after their account was incorrectly de-linked.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Reports to ASIC between 1 September 2023 and 31 August 2025 showed banks paid more than $55 million in customer compensation for offset account failures.

It expects compensation to continue as banks further analyse offset account operations.

ASIC chair Sarah Court said that "when offset accounts don't operate correctly, the harm can be hidden".

"Loan repayments stay the same, while customers unknowingly pay more interest and take longer to repay their loan."

Hue Hwa Au Yong, a senior lecturer in banking and finance at Monash University, said offset accounts are "simple to understand but difficult for customers to verify".

Like an everyday transaction account, offset accounts can be used to deposit and withdraw money.

However, the amount of money in an offset account also reduces the outstanding amount owed on a home loan, which is used to calculate interest.

If a person has $50,000 in their offset account and a $750,000 loan, they will only be charged interest on $700,000.

"So, the issue really is not the product itself, but the system behind it," Yong told SBS News.

"As a bank customer, we can see how much money is in our offset account. But as a borrower, we can't easily verify whether the banking systems are correctly applying it when calculating interest, [which] ... is calculated daily using a quite complex formula and system. "

Australian Banking Association CEO Simon Birmingham told SBS News that offset accounts "can be an effective way for mortgage holders to save on interest and in more than 99 per cent of cases banks were found to manage them correctly".

What do you picture when you imagine a housemate? Someone younger or maybe a student in a cheap rental? Insight explores how the 'typical' share house identity has shifted, with more older Australians now finding themselves in house sharing situations. Watch Insight episode Housemates on SBS On Demand.

When Charlotte, 26, was a university student, she moved in with a man who was also her landlord .

Her first impression of him was positive, but she says she moved in "without being fully aware of what that individual was like".
